title: SBA Loan Servicing: How It Works for Borrowers and Lenders
summary: Lenders service 7(a) loans, CDCs 504s, and SBA services EIDL loans. Learn how to pay, get hardship help, and meet servicing rules.
body_markdown:
SBA loan servicing decides where you pay, who approves changes to your loan, and who answers when cash gets tight. This guide covers both sides: borrowers managing an existing SBA loan, and lenders and CDCs carrying servicing and compliance duties.


SBA policies and contact details change often. Everything below reflects SBA guidance as of November 2026, so confirm details on the live SBA pages before you act.


‍


### What Is SBA Loan Servicing?


SBA loan servicing is everything that happens after an SBA loan funds: collecting payments, tracking balances, handling modifications and servicing actions, monitoring the borrower and collateral, and reporting to the SBA. Who services the loan depends on its type. Lenders service most 7(a) loans and Certified Development Companies (CDCs) service 504 loans, while the SBA services COVID-19 EIDL loans, disaster loans, and loans it has purchased.


The volume is large. According to the U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA 2025 annual report](https://legacy.sba.gov/article/2026/01/20/us-small-business-administration-releases-2025-annual-report) , the agency reported guaranteeing 85,000 7(a) and 504 small business loans for a total of $45 billion in FY25. Each of those loans needs servicing for its full term.


Use this table, based on SBA's payment guidance and SBA lender servicing requirements, to find your SBA loan servicer and where to go for help. It answers the most common question first: who services my SBA loan?


Loan type Who services it Where to pay or get help


7(a) loan Your lender Your lender


504 loan Your CDC Your CDC or lender


PPP loan Your lender Your lender


COVID-19 EIDL SBA SBA Loan Portal or 833-853-5638


Disaster loan SBA SBA Loan Portal or 800-659-2955


7(a), 504, or PPP loan purchased by SBA SBA SBA Loan Portal or the loan servicing center on your statement


Your SBA loan servicer is your main contact for payments, payoff quotes, and servicing actions. If the SBA purchases the guaranty on a lender's loan, the SBA takes over servicing, so check your latest statement before you call.


For lenders and CDCs, the same split defines responsibility. You own servicing, documentation, and reporting on your 7(a) and 504 loans until the SBA steps in.


‍


### How to Manage Your Loan in the SBA Loan Portal


The SBA Loan Portal is where SBA-serviced borrowers view and manage their loans. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA payment guidance](https://www.sba.gov/loans/make-payment-sba/) states that the SBA Loan Portal replaces the Capital Access Financial System (CAFS).


The portal only covers loans the SBA services directly:


- **COVID-19 EIDL:** Managed in the portal.
- **Disaster loans:** Managed in the portal.
- **Guaranty-purchased PPP loans:** Managed in the portal after SBA purchase.
- **Guaranty-purchased SBA-serviced 7(a) loans:** Managed in the portal after SBA purchase.
- **Debenture-purchased 504 loans:** Managed in the portal after SBA purchase.


If your loan isn't on this list, contact your lender. The portal won't show lender-serviced loans.


Log in with your existing CAFS or VetCert credentials. RAPID portal credentials do not work in the SBA Loan Portal.


Once you're in, the portal covers the core borrower tasks:


- **Loan details:** View balances, statements, and payment due dates.
- **Payments:** Make one-time or recurring payments online.
- **Messages:** Send the SBA a message, including a payoff amount request.


To find your SBA loan number, check the top-left corner of your Note and your Loan Authorization and Agreement. Use the loan number, not your application number, since the two are different.


Check your due dates in the portal rather than estimating them. For COVID-19 EIDL loans, the first payment is due 30 months from the date of the Note.


For a closer look at statuses, payments, and documents, read our[SBA loan tracking guide](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-tracking-how-to-check-your-status-payments-and-documents) . It walks through how to access your SBA loan information step by step.


‍


### How to Make SBA Loan Payments


Starting October 1, 2025, the SBA accepts only electronic payments, and checks mailed after that date are returned to the sender, according to SBA's payment guidance above. The change follows The White House's[executive order on federal payments](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/03/modernizing-payments-to-and-from-americas-bank-account/) , which directed Treasury to stop issuing paper checks for federal disbursements effective September 30, 2025.


If you used to pay by check, switch to an electronic method before your next due date. Mailed checks come back to you unprocessed.


To make an SBA loan payment online, log in to the portal and follow three steps:


1. Select **Action** .
2. Select **Payments** .
3. Select **Make payment** .


You can choose between two payment types:


- **One-time payment:** Pay from a bank account, debit card, or PayPal.
- **Recurring payment:** Pay automatically from a bank account or debit card. Recurring debit card payments are limited to 36 months.


To pay by phone, use the SBA loan payment phone number that matches your loan:


- **COVID-19 EIDL:** Call 833-853-5638 (TTY: 711), 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday.
- **Disaster loans:** Call 800-659-2955.


If your lender services your 7(a), 504, or PPP loan, pay your lender directly. The SBA Loan Portal handles only SBA-serviced loans.


‍


### How to Pay Off an SBA Loan in Full


Paying off an SBA loan starts with an exact payoff amount. The process depends on who services your loan.


- **COVID-19 EIDL:** Your payoff includes daily accrued interest plus UCC fees paid. Request your payoff amount by calling 833-853-5638, emailingCOVIDEIDLServicing@sba.gov , or sending a message in the portal.
- **7(a) and 504 loans:** Request your payoff amount from your lender.


If you plan to pay off an EIDL early, request a fresh payoff amount close to your payment date. Interest accrues daily, so the figure changes.


Pay the exact quoted amount through an electronic method. Checks are no longer accepted, so plan your payoff payment through the portal, by phone, or with your lender.


‍


### COVID-19 EIDL Hardship Help and Delinquency


If you need to lower SBA loan payments on a COVID-19 EIDL, the SBA offers a temporary reduction. According to the U.S. Small Business Administration's[COVID EIDL payment assistance](https://www.sba.gov/loans/covid-era-programs/) page, the SBA allows eligible COVID-EIDL borrowers to reduce their payments by 50% for six months.


You can use this EIDL payment assistance once every five years. This option applies only to COVID-19 EIDL loans.


To qualify for the 50% payment reduction, your loan must meet every condition:


- **Delinquency status:** The loan is less than 90 days past due.
- **Account status:** The loan is not charged off or uncollectible.
- **Business status:** Your business is open.
- **Bankruptcy status:** You have no active bankruptcy.
- **Hardship type:** Your hardship is temporary.


Interest is not waived during the reduced-payment period. Unpaid interest builds up, which means a larger balloon payment at the end of the loan.


Weigh that tradeoff before you apply. The reduction eases cash flow for six months, and you repay the difference later.


A delinquent EIDL can move out of SBA's hands. Here's the order of consequences:


- **Treasury Offset Program:** At 120 days of delinquency, your account may be referred to the Treasury Offset Program.
- **Cross-Servicing transfer:** Once your loan transfers to Treasury Cross-Servicing, the SBA no longer services it.
- **Treasury contact:** After transfer, contact Treasury at 800-289-7388.


If you're close to 90 days past due, act early. Payment assistance requires the loan to be less than 90 days past due.


‍


### How to Request an SBA Loan Servicing Action


An SBA servicing action is a change to the terms or structure of your loan. Common requests include:


- **Assumption:** Another party takes over the loan.
- **Change in ownership:** The ownership of the borrowing business changes.
- **Release or substitution of collateral:** Collateral is released or swapped.
- **Release of guarantor:** A guarantor is removed from the loan.
- **Subordination:** SBA's lien priority changes relative to another lien.
- **Relocation:** The business moves to a new location.
- **PMSI or trade-in:** A purchase-money security interest or equipment trade-in affects collateral.
- **General assistance:** Other servicing questions or requests.


For a COVID-19 EIDL, the U.S. Small Business Administration publishes[servicing action requirement letters](https://legacy.sba.gov/funding-programs/loans/covid-19-relief-options/covid-19-economic-injury-disaster-loan/manage-your-eidl) for each action—read the one that matches your request first. Then email your complete request toCOVIDEIDLServicing@sba.gov .


For 7(a) and 504 loans, submit the request through your lender or CDC. Some actions also need SBA approval. A complete request avoids back-and-forth and delays.


Before you send any servicing request, run through a quick check:


- **Right servicer:** Confirm whether the SBA, your lender, or your CDC services the loan.
- **Right requirements:** For a COVID-19 EIDL, match your action to its requirement letter.
- **Complete package:** Include every document the requirement letter or your lender asks for.
- **Right channel:** EmailCOVIDEIDLServicing@sba.gov for COVID-19 EIDL, or contact your lender or CDC for 7(a) and 504.


‍


### What SBA Lenders and CDCs Owe in Servicing


Servicing doesn't end at funding for lenders and CDCs. SBA expects them to service, document, and report on every loan for its full life.


Those obligations scale with portfolio size. Strong operations keep a growing SBA book compliant without adding manual work. The sections below cover the federal servicing standard, current SOP guidance, documentation and 1502 reporting, CDC timelines, and enforcement risk.


#### Servicing Standards and SBA's Right to Take Over


The[federal servicing standard](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/13/120.535) in 13 CFR § 120.535, via Cornell's Legal Information Institute, sets the baseline. Lenders and CDCs must service 7(a) and 504 loans in their portfolio no less diligently than their non-SBA portfolio. Servicing must also be commercially reasonable and follow prudent standards.


The SBA may take over servicing of a loan at its sole discretion. Lenders should treat SBA loan servicing requirements as an ongoing duty.


For 7(a) loans, the U.S. Small Business Administration's[SOP 50 57 4](https://legacy.sba.gov/document/sop-50-57-7a-loan-servicing-liquidation) governs servicing and liquidation, effective November 1, 2025. Older guidance from before that date may be outdated.


#### Documentation, 1502 Reporting, and CDC Timelines


Document every loan action. Each file should include the request, the justification, the analysis, and supporting documents.


Reporting runs monthly. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA lender servicing requirements](https://www.sba.gov/sba-lenders/) state that 7(a) lenders must classify the loan as "In Liquidation" on their monthly SBA Form 1502 Report when they accelerate the note or receive notice that the borrower filed for bankruptcy.


CDCs carry their own timelines:


- **Debenture purchase trigger:** A CDC should ask SBA to purchase the debenture when the loan is 60 or more days past due with no prospect of a deferment or a workout.
- **Site visit report:** CDCs must make a site visit and submit a detailed report to SBA within 15 days of liquidation status.


#### Enforcement Risk for Servicing Gaps


Servicing gaps create enforcement exposure. Under 13 CFR § 120.1400, violating Loan Program Requirements counts as a default.


The[SBA enforcement grounds](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/13/120.1400) in 13 CFR § 120.1400, via Cornell's Legal Information Institute, include not servicing loans prudently. They also include failure to correct an underwriting, closing, disbursing, servicing, liquidation, litigation, or reporting deficiency within the specified time. Under the same regulation, enforcement can include suspension of a lender's authority to service SBA loans.


For lender compliance teams, timely fixes matter as much as accurate files.


#### Scale SBA Servicing Without Growing Overhead


As Lendflow outlines in its guide to[choosing SBA lending software](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-lending-software-how-to-choose-a-platform-that-speeds-decisions-without-adding-headcount) , its embedded finance customers operate with 80% smaller teams while converting similar funding volumes. That is a platform-wide figure across Lendflow's embedded finance customers, rather than an SBA-specific result. Lean operations still matter for SBA servicing, where documentation and reporting load grows with every loan added to the book.

### Who to Contact for SBA Loan Servicing Help


Use this table, compiled from SBA's payment guidance and SBA's COVID-era program page, to reach the right SBA loan servicing center or phone number. Have your loan number ready before you call or email.


Loan or need Contact Details


COVID-19 EIDL SBACESC@sba.gov or 833-853-5638


Disaster loan SBAdisastercustomerservice@sba.gov or 800-659-2955


SBA Loan Portal technical help SBAcls@sba.gov (cannot access loan information)


PPP, 7(a), 504, or Microloan Your lender If SBA purchased the loan, contact the loan servicing center on your statement


Treasury Cross-Servicing U.S. Treasury 800-289-7388


The portal help desk atcls@sba.gov handles login and technical issues only. For balances, payments, or hardship questions, use the loan-specific contact above.


Free or low-cost counseling is also available. SBA Resource Partners and SBA District Offices can help you understand your options.


‍


### Frequently Asked Questions


These answers cover the most common SBA loan servicing questions from borrowers. Confirm details on live SBA pages, since policies change.


#### What is the phone number to make SBA loan payments?


For a COVID-19 EIDL, call 833-853-5638 (TTY: 711). For a disaster loan, call 800-659-2955.


#### How do I make a payment on my SBA loan online?


Log in to the SBA Loan Portal and select Action, then Payments, then Make payment. If your lender services your loan, pay your lender instead.


#### How do I find my SBA loan number?


Log in to the SBA Loan Portal or check the top-left corner of your Note. Your loan number is not the same as your application number.


#### When did SBA stop accepting check payments?


The SBA stopped accepting check payments on October 1, 2025. Checks mailed after that date are returned to the sender.


#### What happens if my SBA EIDL loan becomes delinquent?


At 120 days of delinquency, your account may be referred to the Treasury Offset Program. If your loan transfers to Treasury Cross-Servicing, the SBA no longer services it.


#### Can I request a payment reduction on my SBA loan?


Eligible COVID-19 EIDL borrowers can reduce payments by 50% for six months. For other SBA loans, ask your lender about options.


#### What servicing actions can I request on my SBA loan?


You can request an assumption, ownership change, collateral release or substitution, guarantor release, subordination, or relocation. Submit COVID-19 EIDL requests to the SBA and 7(a) or 504 requests through your lender or CDC.
